items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] This is a fellow named Steven Holden. He said... [INTERVIEWEE] That’s when they used to be able to write in the New York Times.

ctx.x: You know the thing that was interesting about that is I got the assignment, you know, so Bucky came home from Marty’s with Slam and Bucky would go to bed and I would say, and there was Ovaltine and so Slam loved to sit there and there was a table in our kitchen that had a little TV and I would sort of sit there and watch him have cookies and Ovaltine and he would always take a sip and he’d go, “knock out drops, ha-ha-ha-ha.” And he would just say that. And you know the interesting thing about that was I had no…

I have here an article from the New York Times it’s entitled — it’s a review — “A Family Reunion with a Smile” John Pizzarelli at the Regency. And I wanted to read just a short bit from it. This is a fellow named Steven Holden. He said, “For all the whimsy he weaves into his music, the jokes and references never devolve into comic shtick but embody his view of music-making as intellectual and aesthetic play.
That’s when they used to be able to write in the New York Times.
